text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--Second biggest Danish insurance group Codan did better than its two main competitors Tryg-Baltica and Topdanmark in 1996, emerging from the year with the lowest combined ratio of 100.8, although third-biggest Topdanmark gained a bigger share of the accident, life and pension insurance markets.
--Danish state rail's shipping unit DSB Rederi swung into a 387.5 million crown profit in 1996 compared to the previous year's 51.2 million crown shortfall.

--Danish collective wage negotiations for 1997 resulted in pay rises of between 3.5-4.0 percent, with local deals still to be worked out. The rises were higher than in the main EU nations with which Denmark competes, sparking fears of a loss of Danish export competitiveness.

--Stalled negotiations on deregulation of the telecommunications industry in Denmark seem set to restart between the government and the opposition Liberals and Conservatives if the former can gain assurances from the European Union that its draft liberalisation bill is not in conflict with Brussels.

--Royal Copenhagen porcelain has opened a new shop in a fashionable quarter of Tokyo as part of a major campaign to focus on the Japanese market. Royal Copenhagen has now a total of 72 shops in Japan, Taiwan, Hong Kong, South Korea and Singapore and is currently opening two new outlets per quarter in the region.
--Denmark's powerful Metal union has joined in the chorus of strong industrial opposition to government plans for industry to finance pools of jobs for the handicapped and disabled.
